findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and why it matters, all in plain words. It does its job.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The next step is linked from the header. The Next steps section gives prerequisites, a clone command, `./setup.sh`, and a first command (`athena ask "add a changelog"`), so the newcomer knows what to do.
findings.source: Header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: The second section on the page is an error message. The lede promises a commit traced to the models, cost and verdict, and this was the place to show it. A newcomer sees no example of that, and the page looks broken.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The page is at Athena's own address, but the title and almost all of the body are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to read three header paragraphs to understand why.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: Most of the page is a dense state-machine study of firstmate, with exit codes, guards and claim ids. It shows what Athena can do, but someone deciding whether to try Athena gets nothing from reading it closely and may give up.
findings.source: Sections States of a piece of work, Counters, Transitions (t1–t12), Why it is built this way, Glossary, Claims and sources (c1–c45)

findings.text: This link speaks to the repository owner, not to a visitor. A newcomer cannot tell whether it is meant for them.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Several terms are defined twice, once near the top and again in the Glossary, in almost the same words. That makes an already long page longer.
findings.source: Words used first and Glossary: the entries for in scope, yolo, green, red, home, captain

findings.text: The page says plainly that nothing was run. A careful reader learns that the claims come from reading the source, not from watching it work.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "This study read the pinned tree only... no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."

findings.text: This is a detail of how the site is built. It means nothing to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
